chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Comparing the Keppard band with the Original Dixieland Jazz Band
summary: He praises the ODJB's control and Tiger Rag, says Keppard's band might have been better but never recorded, and says he heard one in a cabaret and the other on record.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. What kind of music were they playing. Was this kind of a ragtime, was it?
What I would call today, it was not ragtime, it was real swing.
Well, by this time the Original Dixieland Jazz Band had made those records.
Briggs
Yes, yes.
Was it pretty much along those same lines?
To a certain extent, yes.
What would be the differences?
The difference is I would say that Nick LaRocca, an awfully nice trumpet player -- He played cornet, I think.
Yes.
What you call the trumpet-cornet. And Larry Shields was an excellent clarinetist. Outside of his style.
Right.
As an instrumentalist, you know.
Right.
I think that -- I don't care about making comparisons, but I believe that -- 'cause I heard a recording of
Briggs
the Dixieland, and I think they're awfully good.
Yeh.
And I heard 'Tiger Rag,' and I think it was very, very good. Very good. And not only very good, I mean classy.
Well, the men had total control of their instruments.
Right.
I'm not casting aspersions against others, but I'm just saying 'cause some had opportunities that others have not had.
Right.
You see, that's the way I've always thought in life. That's why I'm always offering a hand, a helping hand.
Right.
And I was never so enthused with the Dixieland's 'Tiger Rag,' --
That had quite a
Briggs
That sure did. It was simply terrific. They had a wonderful break, but they deserved it.
But surely the Keppard band was really a better band, wasn't it?

It might have been, because the Keppard band had never had an opportunity to record, and maybe the recordings-- I mean the technique, the technique of recording at the time that Keppard made his recordings, the technique might not have been as good as the others. Vice-versa, you can never tell. It comes from one thing, either the technique or it comes from the technique of the man, the capacity of the man.
Well, did you have a feeling that the Keppard band was any different in any way from the Original Dixieland Jazz Band?
Briggs
Well, yes.-- no, the point is I couldn't make any comparison of the two because I heard Keppard's band in a cabaret, a noisy cabaret, you see. And I heard the Dixieland on a victrola.
Right.
But I think that they're both good.
Right.
Freddie Keppard, himself, was interested in the others so much, he invested so much.
